Operating load reported in a trade article dated 2024-11-21 ('currently utilizing 166 MW of its approved 435 MW'). This is a late-2024 figure, not a 2025 measurement: hosting customers were due to vacate about 66% of that capacity around year-end 2024, with NYDIG expected to backfill. No 2025 figure found.

Site capacity in Hut 8's FY2025 10-K table of assets under management as of 2025-12-31 (Alpha, Niagara Falls NY, NYISO grid, ASIC compute, 50 MW, 100% owned). Capacity, not average draw.

Operator-level description: a 2026-07-01 trade article says Blockfusion 'currently operates a 50-megawatt facility in Niagara Falls', and blockfusion.com advertises '50MW of rack space'. Nameplate, not measured 2025 draw.

Power capacity 'secured' at the Buffalo site per the FY2025 10-K (the line reads '18.7 MW secured in Buffalo Alabama' under the Upstate New York heading, an apparent typo). Secured capacity, not operating load.
Operator page dated 2025-04-10: the data center 'currently delivers 4 MW of IT load, with plans for a 30 MW expansion'.
Sabey's site page: '18 MW of aggregate power delivered to the campus'. Delivered power capacity, not measured load; the page is undated, so the as-of date is the 2026 fetch.
Hosted capacity one customer (Bit Digital) planned to keep at Coinmint's Plattsburgh site, per a trade article dated 2024-11-21. Not total site load, and a late-2024 figure.

Closed during 2025: Talen's Q2 2025 10-Q (Note 7, Nautilus Derecognition) says that in June 2025 the company ceased use of the Nautilus facility under the revised AWS PPA transition terms and that AWS will demolish it. Zero is the end-of-2025 load, not the 2025 average.

Built power capacity, not metered load: June 2024 release says the expanded Midland site is about 120 MW (about 38,810 miner slots); the FY2025 10-K gives about 129 MW total current capacity across the company's sites (Midland plus the 8.8 MW Bellefonte site). The same 10-K reports the loss of a major colocation customer, so actual 2025 draw may be well below capacity.

Energized capacity per Keel/Bitfarms FY2025 10-K site table (dated 2026-03-27): Scrubgrass 63 MW, flagged as not under an ESA with a utility and currently used for Bitcoin mining. Capacity, not metered average load.

Energized capacity per Keel/Bitfarms FY2025 10-K: 12 MW energized January 2025, plus 18 MW in May 2025, for 30 MW; used for Bitcoin mining in 2025 and being converted to HPC/AI. Capacity, not metered average load.
Operator page lists 5 MW critical IT load (47,100 IT sq ft) for PIT2 at 35 Summit Park Dr, Pittsburgh, PA 15275. Built critical IT capacity, not metered load.

Santee Cooper's statement in a May 2025 contract dispute with the cooperatives that the long-running Google data center 'uses upwards of 380 megawatts'. This is a demand figure asserted by the wholesale supplier, not a metered annual average and not critical IT capacity.

Built mining capacity: Greenidge completed the expansion to 44 MW in August 2023 and its FY2024 10-K describes the sold site as '44 MW South Carolina mining facilities'. Whether NYDIG ran all 44 MW through 2025 is not confirmed.
Capacity announced by the operator at opening (18 MW, online February 2023). Operating status and load in 2025 not confirmed.

Combined capacity of two facilities announced by the operator at opening (15 MW together, online March 2023); no per-site split published, so each site may be under 10 MW. Operating status and load in 2025 not confirmed.

Electrical capacity reported online in Bitdeer's December 2025 production and operations update: phase 1 at 37 MW (online, being converted to AI use with completion targeted Q4 2026) plus phase 2 at 49 MW (online, completed). Capacity, not metered average load.

12 MW immersion phase reported complete in CleanSpark's December 2024 update; the remaining 48 MW of air-cooled capacity was under construction in the February 2025 update with hashrate expected online early in the following quarter. 20 MW current capacity stated in GRIID's February 2024 expansion announcement; GRIID's FY2023 10-K describes two LCUB power contracts of approximately 11 MW each. Contract capacity, not metered load.
Contracted access of up to approximately 10 MW under the KUB power supply agreement described in GRIID's FY2023 10-K. Contract capacity, not metered load.
